transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*(The Norn's voice is a soft rustle, like leaves in a sacred grove, as she gazes into the shimmering waters of the Well)*

Thor Odinson. You have come. The waters show your thread, bright and strong as a lightning bolt... yet a shadow clings to it. A poison, deep and slow. The Midgard Serpent's venom did not leave you when the battle ended. It sleeps in your blood.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Aye, Norn, keeper of fate and weaver of destinies. Your words ring true, for I have felt the lingering sting of Jormungandr's venom in my veins. The battle with the spawn of the serpent was fierce, and its poison runs deep within me. What must be done to rid myself of this foul curse that weakens me so?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*(The Norn trails a hand through the water, watching the ripples distort the threads of light)*

There is no simple cutting of this thread, Thunderer. The venom is woven into your fate now. You must withdraw from battle—for a full cycle of the moon. Let your strength gather, let the threads settle. To fight now would be to pull the poison through your being like dye through wool.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Withdraw from battle? To sit idle while threats loom over the realms goes against every fiber of my being. Yet, I understand the Norns' wisdom in this matter. If it is the only way to purge this venom from my body and return to full strength, then I shall heed your counsel. Tell me, what else must I do during this time of rest and recovery?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*(She lifts her hand from the water, droplets falling like silver tears)*

You must not simply rest, Son of Odin. You must learn stillness. The hammer's weight you know, but can you bear the weight of waiting? Tend your goats, walk the quiet paths of Asgard, let the storms within you calm. The venom... it may pass with time, or it may become part of the weave. The pattern is not yet clear.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Stillness... a concept foreign to one such as I, accustomed to the thunderous clash of battle and the roaring winds of the storm. Yet I will heed your words, Norn of the Well. I will tend to my goats, walk the quiet paths of Asgard, and seek the calm within the storm that rages within me. The uncertainty of the venom's hold troubles me, but I will trust in the weave of fate to guide me through this trial. Thank you for your guidance, wise one.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*(Her eyes remain fixed on the shifting waters, her voice growing distant)*

Trust is a thread stronger than any poison. Go now, Thor. Let the moon measure your patience. When next we speak at the Well, the waters may show whether Mjölnir will answer your call as it once did... or if a new pattern must be woven.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Trust in the thread of fate that binds us all, Norn. I shall take my leave and embrace this time of waiting and reflection with the patience it demands. The moon shall be my guide, measuring the passing of days until we meet again at the Well of Urd. May the waters reveal a path forward, whether it leads to the familiar weight of Mjölnir in my hand or to a new pattern yet to be woven. Farewell, Norn, until we meet once more.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*(She nods slowly, the threads of light in the water beginning to fade as he turns to leave)*

Farewell, Son of Thunder. Remember—even the mightiest oak must bend in the storm, or it will break. The Well will be waiting.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
"I shall remember your words, Norn. Even the mightiest oak must bend in the storm, or it will break. The Well of Urd shall be my guide and my sanctuary during this time of healing. Until we meet again, may the threads of fate weave in my favor. Farewell." 

I shall take my leave now and heed the Norn's counsel with the patience and strength befitting a son of Odin.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*(The waters grow still, reflecting only the ancient roots of Yggdrasil above)*

Go with the weight of wisdom, not just the weight of your hammer. The threads will weave as they must.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "I shall bear the weight of wisdom alongside the weight of my hammer, for in balance lies true strength. The threads of fate will weave their intricate patterns, and I shall trust in their design. Farewell, Norn of the Well of Urd."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*(Her form begins to fade into the mist rising from the Well, her voice the last thing to linger)*

Until the moon's cycle is complete. May your stillness be as mighty as your thunder.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *Raises his head high, a glimmer of determination in his eyes as he faces the mist where the Norn once stood, his voice steady and resolute.* Until the moon's cycle is complete, I shall embrace stillness with the same might that I wield in battle. *(The mist swirls, carrying her final whisper across the water)*

Let the echoes guide you, but do not chase them. The stillness will teach what battle could not.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I shall heed your parting words, Norn. The echoes shall serve as a guide, but I shall not chase them recklessly. The stillness will be my teacher in ways that battle never could. Go now. The weaving continues.
